about.title: Built for people who won't sit still
body: OrthoEdge was founded by two former college athletes turned orthopedic surgeons who were frustrated by how little emphasis mainstream ortho practices put on getting back to actual performance, not just pain-free daily life.
Every treatment plan here includes a rehab and return-to-sport timeline from day one — not just a surgery date.

blogPosts.title: Return to Sport Should Be a Test, Not Just a Calendar Date
blogPosts.excerpt: Why time-based clearance after an injury misses the point — and what objective testing actually looks like.
blogPosts.author: Dr. Owen Mackay
content: "Six months post-ACL surgery" is a starting point for a conversation about return to sport, not an answer — recovery speed varies enormously between individuals.
Objective testing — strength symmetry, hop tests, movement quality under fatigue — tells you far more about re-injury risk than a date on a calendar.
Athletes cleared purely on a time-based schedule have meaningfully higher re-injury rates than those cleared based on performance benchmarks.
If your clinic hasn't tested your actual performance before clearing you to play, it's worth asking why.
